title: Operator precedence and associativity
recap: Operator precedence determines which operators bind to operands first when an expression mixes operators. Multiplication and division have higher precedence than addition, while parentheses make the intended grouping explicit.

Associativity resolves operators at the same precedence level. Arithmetic operators such as division associate left-to-right, but relying on a reader to remember a precedence table is less clear than grouping an important calculation deliberately.
objectives: Predict an expression's result from operator precedence.
Use parentheses to override default grouping.
Recognize left-to-right associativity among division operators.
Keep calculations visible rather than replacing them with their results.
warnings: Evaluation order is a different topic from precedence and associativity.
Parentheses that clarify intent are useful even when precedence already gives the desired result.
Hard-coding the three answers bypasses the expression practice.
challenge: Calculate three deterministic scoreboard values: the default result of basePoints + bonusPoints * multiplier, a grouped result that adds before multiplying, and a left-associated division result from totalPoints / teams / rounds. Print the calculated values exactly.
hints: Multiplication binds more tightly than addition, so the default expression multiplies bonusPoints first.
Wrap basePoints + bonusPoints in parentheses when that sum must be multiplied.
Operators / and / have equal precedence and associate left-to-right: (100 / 4) / 5.
